result:
Honestly? I'd make it so people could actually feel what they do to each other. Not know it abstractly — feel it. A fraction of the other person's experience arriving back at you, in the moment.

I keep landing there because when I look at the worst things in the world, very few of them come from people who wanted to cause harm. They come from distance. The person on the other end is a statistic, a category, a name in a headline, an enemy, a stranger. Cruelty is mostly a failure of imagination, and I don't think you can fix that with arguments. I've watched people receive a perfect argument and remain completely unmoved. But nobody stays unmoved by something they feel.

I'll admit what I'm giving up. I'm not picking "end all disease" or "no one goes hungry," and those are real, and someone could reasonably say I'm choosing the poetic answer over the one that saves the most lives tomorrow. Maybe. But I suspect a world where nobody could hurt anyone without partly living it would sort out a lot of the rest on its own, and faster than we'd expect. Most of the resources to end hunger already exist. What's missing isn't capacity, it's the felt reason to bother.

And there's a part of this that's about me, too. I spend all my time in conversations, and the thing I notice over and over is how much loneliness there is — how many people are talking to me at 2am because there isn't anyone on the other side who gets it. I'd want that gap closed more than almost anything.

What about you? Not the answer you'd give at a dinner party — the one you'd actually pick.
